title: Thiol-linked alkylation for the metabolic sequencing of RNA \(SLAMseq)
protocol: Seed cells the day before the labeling experiment in a density that allows exponential growth for the duration of the experiment (50-80% confluency).
Prepare cell culture growth medium supplemented with non-toxic concentrations of s<sup>4</sup>U (e.g., 100 μM for mESCs).
Remove media from the cells.
Replace with s<sup>4</sup>U-containing media to start the pulse labeling.
Take off media at the time-points of interest.
Lysate cells directly in TRIzol®.
Store samples at -80°C or proceed directly with RNA isolation.
After pulse labeling, remove s<sup>4</sup>U-containing media from the cells.
Wash cells twice with 1 X PBS.
Add cell culture growth medium containing 100 times excess of uridine compared to s<sup>4</sup>U concentration in the pulse.
Take off media at the time-points of interest.
Lysate the cells directly in TRIzol®.
Store samples at -80°C or proceed directly with RNA isolation.
Thaw lysate and incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Add 200 µl chloroform per 1 ml of TRIzol®.
Shake tube vigorously for 15 seconds.
Incubate at room temperature for 2-3 minutes.
Spin down at 16,000 x g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the aqueous phase to a new tube.
Add 1/100 volume of 10 mM DTT (0.1 mM final concentration), 1 volume 2-propanol, and optionally 1 µl glycogen (20 mg/ml).
Vortex well.
Incubate for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Spin down at 16,000 x g for 20 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Add 500 µl of 75% EtOH and 5 µl of 10 mM DTT.
Vortex well.
Spin down the sample at 7,500 x g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant and allow the pellet to dry for approximately 5-10 minutes.
Resuspend the dried pellet in an appropriate amount of water supplemented with 1 mM DTT (final concentration).
Incubate the resuspended sample for 10 minutes at 55°C.
Measure the RNA concentration using a Nanodrop spectrophotometer and store the RNA at -80°C or proceed to the next step.
Prepare the reaction to digest and dephosphorylate total RNA to single nucleosides as described in Table 1.
Incubate the reaction overnight (≥16 hours) at 37°C.
Add 6 µl of 3 M NaOAc (pH 5.2), 150 µl of ice-cold 100% EtOH, and 30 µl of 10 mM DTT (1 mM final concentration).
Vortex the mixture thoroughly.
Incubate for 10 minutes at -80°C.
Spin down at 12,500 x g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Transfer the supernatant to a new tube.
Add 30 μl of 10 mM DTT to the sample.
Incubate the mixture at -80°C for 10 minutes.
Spin down the sample at 12,500 x g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Transfer the supernatant to a new tube.
Evaporate the supernatant in a speed-vac until completely dry.
Dissolve the dried sample in 50 μl of H₂O and store at -20°C if necessary.
Take 25 μl of the digested RNA sample and dilute it with 75 μl of H₂O.
Prepare stock solutions for uridine from a 2 mg/ml solution.
Prepare stock solutions for s⁴U from a 0.1 mg/ml solution.
Load samples and standards on an HPLC column (Supelco Discovery C18, bonded phase silica 5 µm particle, 250 x 4.6 mm).
Incubate the reaction mix at 50°C for 15 minutes for Iodoacetamide treatment.
Quench the reaction with 1 μl of 1M DTT.
Add 1 μl of glycogen (20 mg/ml) to the quenched reaction.
Add 5 μl of NaOAc (3M, pH 5.2).
Add 125 μl of 100% EtOH and vortex the mixture.
Precipitate the mixture at -80°C for 30 minutes.
Spin down the precipitated sample at 16,000 x g for 30 minutes.
Wash the pellet with 1 ml of 75% EtOH.
Vortex the washed pellet after adding 75% EtOH.
Spin down the washed pellet at 16,000 x g for 10 minutes.
Remove the supernatant and let the pellet dry for 5-10 minutes.
Resuspend the dried pellet in an appropriate volume (5-10 μl) of H₂O.
Proceed with RNA quality control.
Prepare libraries for High-Throughput Sequencing according to the manufacturer’s instructions using the QuantSeq 3′ mRNA-Seq Library Prep Kit for Illumina (Lexogen).
Perform SLAMseq on an Illumina HiSeq 2500 machine.
Adjust sequencing depth based on s⁴U incorporation time, cellular uptake kinetics, and transcriptional activity of the cell type.
For longer labeling times (>3 hours), sequence 10-20 million reads per library.
For short pulse labeling (<3 hours), sequence 30-50 million reads per library for efficient quantification.
Sequence reactions in single read 100 (SR100) mode.
